status: Draft editorial content; not loaded into firmware or approved for hardware layout.

collections.title: Agent Workflow
collections.description: An optional cross-theme collection for supervising CLI coding agents. These are adaptations of existing cards, not extra cards or a ninth theme.

themes.label: Clarify
themes.need: We're not sure what we're solving.

themes.label: Experiment
themes.need: We need something small to try.

themes.label: Decide
themes.need: We need to choose and move.

cards.title: SCOUT
cards.action: Ask AI for three very different approaches.
cards.question: What would a genuinely different approach look like?
cards.activity: Name the current approach. Ask for three alternatives with different starting assumptions, then choose one difference worth exploring. Do not select a winner yet.
cards.ai_prompt: For this non-sensitive challenge: [challenge], suggest three approaches with different starting assumptions. State each assumption and one trade-off. Avoid three minor variations of the same idea.

facilitator.ask: What different approaches have you considered?
notice: Explore their thinking before adding another option.
follow_ups: What appeals to you about those approaches?
facilitator.try_invitation: Would it help to explore three different approaches?
try_notice: Look for a useful difference between the options. The team can reject AI suggestions or decide not to use AI.
try_follow_ups: Which difference is worth exploring next?
What would you want to learn before choosing?
facilitator.optional_ai_help: AI could suggest contrasting approaches, explaining the assumptions and tradeoffs—not just variations of the same idea.

cards.title: NEW PERSPECTIVE
cards.action: Ask AI to critique the idea as its intended user.
cards.question: What might the person using this find difficult?
cards.activity: Describe an intended user without identifying them. Ask AI for possible difficulties, then separate plausible concerns from guesses. Choose one question to ask a real user; simulated feedback is not user research.
cards.ai_prompt: Review this idea: [idea], for this intended user: [generic needs]. Suggest possible frustrations and label them as hypotheses, not real user feedback. Give one question we could ask an actual user.

cards.title: SIDE TRAIL
cards.action: Borrow an approach from a different field. Name where the analogy breaks.
cards.question: Who solves a similar problem in a very different setting?
cards.activity: Pick a different field, such as libraries or gardening. Borrow one useful pattern for the challenge. Name one important difference that makes the analogy unreliable, then keep only the useful part.
cards.ai_prompt: For [challenge], suggest an analogy from another field. Explain one transferable pattern and one important limit of the analogy. Do not treat the analogy as evidence.

cards.title: HUMAN FIRST
cards.action: Sketch how to solve the problem without AI. Keeping that approach is a complete choice.
cards.question: What would we do if AI were unavailable?
cards.activity: Draw a three-step human-only workflow. Keeping it is a complete choice. If useful, compare a limited AI-assisted or hybrid option, including preparation, checking, corrections and learning value. Keep accountable human judgment visible; do not assume AI adds value.
cards.ai_prompt: Here is a human-only workflow: [steps]. Suggest one limited place AI might help and one reason not to use it. Keep the accountable human decision visible.

facilitator.try_invitation: Would it help to sketch a human-only approach?
try_notice: Keeping the human-only approach is complete. Any comparison with AI is optional and includes checking and learning value.
try_follow_ups: What would you keep about this approach?
facilitator.ask: How would you approach this without AI?
notice: Keeping that approach is a complete, legitimate outcome.
follow_ups: What do you like about doing it that way?
facilitator.optional_ai_help: Compare human-only, AI-assisted, and hybrid approaches—including preparation, checking, corrections, and learning value—not just generation speed.

cards.title: WIDER HORIZON
cards.action: Choose one constraint to relax and one to keep. Explore what becomes possible.
cards.question: Which constraint is real, and which have we simply assumed?
cards.activity: List three constraints. Mark which are confirmed and which are assumptions. Temporarily relax one assumption, not a safety or privacy requirement, and sketch a new option.
cards.ai_prompt: For [challenge], we must keep [non-negotiable constraint]. If we relaxed [assumed constraint], what new approach becomes possible? State what would need checking before using it.

cards.title: FOG AHEAD
cards.action: Ask AI to ask you one clarifying question at a time.
cards.question: Which unanswered question would most change our next step?
cards.activity: Give a short, non-sensitive challenge description. Answer up to three clarifying questions, one at a time. Stop and rewrite the challenge using what changed; do not let questioning replace action.
cards.ai_prompt: Help clarify this challenge: [challenge]. Ask one question at a time, starting with the answer most likely to change the approach. After three questions, help me restate the challenge without inventing missing facts.

facilitator.ask: What are you hoping to accomplish?
notice: Let them define the goal before discussing tools or solutions.
follow_ups: What would a useful result let you do?
facilitator.try_invitation: Would one clarifying question at a time help?
try_notice: Notice whether the questions change the team's understanding. Stop when enough is clear to take a useful step; more questions are not always better.
try_follow_ups: What became clearer?
What can you try with what you know now?
facilitator.optional_ai_help: AI could help clarify the task or explain an unfamiliar part, one question at a time.

cards.title: MAP THE GAPS
cards.action: Ask AI to separate known facts from its assumptions.
cards.question: What did we supply as evidence, and what is being filled in?
cards.activity: Take one AI answer. Mark claims grounded in the supplied material, assumptions and unanswered questions. Have a person check those labels against the original material; AI's own labels are not verification.
cards.ai_prompt: Using only this supplied material: [material], separate supported claims, assumptions and open questions in this answer: [answer]. Quote short supporting passages where available. Say when support is missing.

agent_workflow.label: Read the terrain
agent_workflow.prompt: Inspect this repository before editing. Explain the relevant files, active project instructions, existing behavior and uncertainties. Cite file paths. Do not change files or execute project scripts yet.
agent_workflow.check: A person can identify the relevant files and assumptions; no edits or project-script execution occurred.

tool_notes.codex: Ask Codex to identify the applicable AGENTS.md guidance and any overrides before proposing changes.
tool_notes.claude_code: Ask Claude Code which project instructions are active. Check the installed version and settings rather than assuming how CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md interact.

cards.title: SHOW THE TARGET
cards.action: Give AI an example of what a good answer looks like.
cards.question: What makes this example useful rather than merely polished?
cards.activity: Use a non-sensitive example of a useful output. Name two qualities to preserve and one thing not to copy. Ask AI to apply the qualities to a new task, then check the result against them.
cards.ai_prompt: Here is a non-sensitive example: [example]. For [new task], preserve these qualities: [qualities], but do not copy [detail]. Produce a new answer and flag missing inputs.

facilitator.try_invitation: Would it help to try those qualities in a small new example?
try_notice: Notice whether the qualities help with the new task, not just whether the output looks polished.
try_follow_ups: Which qualities carried over, and what would you change?
facilitator.ask: What makes this example useful for what you want to do?
notice: Explore usefulness rather than polish. They may value something you would overlook.
follow_ups: Which qualities would you want to carry into your own work?
facilitator.optional_ai_help: AI could explain those qualities, then demonstrate applying them to a small new example—without copying unnecessary details.

cards.title: NAME THE DESTINATION
cards.action: State who needs what outcome, and how you will notice it helped.
cards.question: Who is this for, and what should be different afterward?
cards.activity: Complete: For [role], we want [outcome], so they can [benefit]. Choose one observable sign of progress and one thing outside scope. Let the team correct the sentence before using AI.
cards.ai_prompt: Help tighten this outcome statement: [statement]. Ask about ambiguous terms and suggest one observable sign of progress. Do not invent user needs or numerical targets.

cards.title: UNPACK THE WORD
cards.action: Pick one vague word in the request. Replace it with an observable requirement.
cards.question: What would better, faster or useful look like in practice?
cards.activity: Circle one vague word in the task. Ask two people to explain what they mean by it, with passing allowed. Agree on a concrete example and a non-example, then rewrite the request.
cards.ai_prompt: In this request: [request], identify one ambiguous term. Suggest two possible interpretations and ask us which we mean. Wait before rewriting the request.

cards.title: SMALL STEPS
cards.action: Ask AI for a test you can finish in ten minutes.
cards.question: What can we learn with a small, safe test rather than a full build?
cards.activity: Choose one uncertain assumption. Define a reversible test with an observable result and a stop condition. Use synthetic or approved material, run the test, and record what it did and did not show.
cards.ai_prompt: Propose a safe, reversible test of [assumption] that takes at most ten minutes using synthetic data. State the steps, observable result and stop condition. Do not treat a small test as proof of general success.

agent_workflow.label: Set the boundary
agent_workflow.prompt: Implement only [agreed step] within [allowed scope]. Leave unrelated files alone. Ask before adding dependencies, changing configuration, accessing external services or taking destructive actions. Stop if the boundary prevents a correct solution.
agent_workflow.check: The diff matches the agreed step, and scope changes were raised rather than silently included.

tool_notes.codex: Inspect the actual Codex sandbox and approval settings before starting. A narrow prompt supplements technical controls; it does not replace them.
tool_notes.claude_code: Inspect Claude Code permissions before starting. Keep action approvals appropriate to the exercise rather than disabling safeguards to avoid interruptions.

facilitator.ask: What would be useful to learn from your next attempt?
notice: Stay with what they want to discover, rather than choosing the experiment for them.
follow_ups: What could you try that would help you find out?
facilitator.try_invitation: Would a small, safe test help you learn more?
try_notice: Look for an actual observation, a safe stopping point and the limits of the test. Finishing a test does not prove the whole idea works.
try_follow_ups: What did you observe?
What can you conclude, and what remains uncertain?
facilitator.optional_ai_help: AI could help plan or build a small, reversible test, with an observable result and a stopping point.

cards.title: FALSE SUMMIT
cards.action: Ask: How could this fail? Test one failure mode.
cards.question: Which plausible failure could we safely expose now?
cards.activity: List possible failures and choose one low-risk case. Test with synthetic input in a sandbox or on paper. Stop if testing would affect real users, private data or live systems.
cards.ai_prompt: For [idea], list three plausible failure modes. Propose a small sandbox test of one using synthetic inputs. Include a stop condition and avoid actions against real users or live systems.

cards.title: ONE VARIABLE
cards.action: Change one part of a prompt. Compare the outputs against the same criterion.
cards.question: What changed, and can we reasonably connect it to this one difference?
cards.activity: Keep the task and input fixed. Change one prompt instruction, compare results against one agreed criterion and note variability. One comparison is a clue, not a reliable performance estimate.
cards.ai_prompt: For this task: [task], propose two prompts differing in exactly one instruction. Name the difference and one criterion for comparing their outputs. Do not predict a winner.

agent_workflow.label: Compare the approach
agent_workflow.prompt: In your separate practice copy, solve [small task] against [shared acceptance checks]. Stay within [scope]. Report the diff and executed checks. Do not edit another agent's working copy or commit and push without approval.
agent_workflow.check: Both attempts start from the same baseline in separate copies. Compare observable results, trade-offs and review effort, not writing style.

tool_notes.codex: Use a separate practice copy for Codex. Record the selected version and model locally so comparison limits are visible.
tool_notes.claude_code: Use a separate practice copy for Claude Code with the same baseline and task. Different settings and models limit what a single comparison can establish.

cards.title: TRAIL SAMPLE
cards.action: Try the same task on an ordinary, an edge and an incomplete example.
cards.question: Does our idea still help when the input is awkward or incomplete?
cards.activity: Prepare three synthetic examples: ordinary, edge case and missing important information. Decide expected behavior before trying them. Check whether the system asks for missing information rather than guessing.
cards.ai_prompt: Create three clearly synthetic inputs for [task]: ordinary, edge case and incomplete. For each, describe the behavior a human reviewer should look for, including when clarification is needed.

cards.title: PAPER BRIDGE
cards.action: Act out a workflow on paper before connecting tools or automating it.
cards.question: Where should a person review or stop this workflow?
cards.activity: Sketch the input, proposed AI step, human review and final action. Walk through one synthetic example. Mark where permission, correction or stopping is needed before building any integration.
cards.ai_prompt: For [workflow], sketch a paper prototype with input, AI suggestion, human review and final action. Identify a permission gate and a safe stopping point. Do not execute any actions.

cards.title: CHECK BEARINGS
cards.action: Which claims need checking? Verify one independently.
cards.question: Which claim would matter most if it were wrong?
cards.activity: Select one consequential factual claim. Use AI or tools if helpful to check original sources, direct observations or trusted references. Look for actual evidence, not model agreement. If you cannot check it now, label it unverified and do not use it to justify a risky action.
cards.ai_prompt: From this answer: [answer], identify consequential factual claims and help locate supporting sources or run suitable checks. Show actual evidence and uncertainty. Do not invent citations, sources or verification results; model agreement is not verification.

agent_workflow.label: Show the evidence
agent_workflow.prompt: Run the agreed, reviewed checks using [approved commands]. Report each command, observed result and any checks not run. Distinguish test evidence from assumptions and stop for approval if a command exceeds scope.
agent_workflow.check: The team can see real check results, including failures and gaps, rather than only a confident completion summary.

tool_notes.codex: Ask Codex to distinguish commands it executed from commands it merely recommends. Independently inspect consequential results.
tool_notes.claude_code: Ask Claude Code to distinguish executed checks from suggested checks. Missing dependencies or denied permissions are limitations, not passing tests.

facilitator.ask: Which part would matter most if it were wrong?
notice: Understand how they intend to use the result. Checking everything is not automatically necessary.
follow_ups: What evidence would be enough for that use?
facilitator.try_invitation: Would it help to check one claim together?
try_notice: Look for an original source, direct observation or trusted reference. A repeated AI answer is not an independent check. Unavailable checks leave a claim unverified.
try_follow_ups: What did the check establish?
What remains unverified?
facilitator.optional_ai_help: AI could identify important claims, locate supporting material, or help run suitable checks. Look for actual evidence, not another confident answer.

cards.title: FOLLOW THE SOURCE
cards.action: Open one cited source. Check that it exists and supports the actual claim.
cards.question: Does this source support these words, or only a nearby topic?
cards.activity: Inspect an original cited source, including its context and applicability. Compare it with the exact claim. If unavailable, mark the claim unverified; do not accept a convincing-looking citation alone.
cards.ai_prompt: Using only this supplied source excerpt: [excerpt], assess support for this claim: [claim]. Separate supported, unsupported and uncertain parts. Do not invent missing source content.

cards.title: FIND THE EXCEPTION
cards.action: Look for a counterexample before treating an attractive claim as a rule.
cards.question: What plausible case would make this claim fail?
cards.activity: Rewrite the claim so it can be checked. Suggest a counterexample and test it against supplied evidence or a safe direct check. If it fails, narrow the claim; if it survives, do not call that proof.
cards.ai_prompt: For this claim: [claim], suggest a plausible counterexample and what evidence would test it. Clearly label hypothetical examples. Do not claim the test has been run.

cards.title: MEASURE TWICE
cards.action: Recheck one number with a calculator or code. Include units and assumptions.
cards.question: Are the inputs, units and calculation all correct?
cards.activity: Select a consequential number. Trace its inputs, recalculate independently using a calculator or code, and check units and rounding. A matching calculation cannot rescue unreliable inputs.
cards.ai_prompt: For this numerical claim: [claim], list the inputs, units, assumptions and calculation needed for an independent check. Mark missing inputs. Do not claim calculator verification unless a tool was actually used.

cards.title: SAFE TO SHARE
cards.action: Before submitting a prompt, remove private details and use synthetic examples where possible.
cards.question: What information does this task really require us to share?
cards.activity: Review the proposed input locally before sending anything. Remove identifying, confidential and unnecessary details; follow the tool's approved-use policy. If unsure, use a synthetic example or do not submit it.
cards.ai_prompt: Help with this clearly synthetic example: [synthetic example]. Do not request real names, credentials, private records or confidential material. Explain what additional non-sensitive context would help.

agent_workflow.label: Permission pause
agent_workflow.prompt: Before taking [proposed action], explain what it reads or changes, any external access, the scope of permission needed and how we could recover. Wait for a decision. Do not reveal credentials or read private files to justify the request.
agent_workflow.check: The human understands the proposed side effects and approves only the intended scope; refusal does not trigger a workaround.

tool_notes.codex: Review the actual Codex request and configured controls. Do not solve a denied action by switching to an unrestricted mode.
tool_notes.claude_code: Read the actual Claude Code permission request before approving. If denied, choose a permitted alternative or stop; do not bypass the control.

cards.title: LEAVE MARKERS
cards.action: Save a useful prompt. Explain why it helped.
cards.question: Which part of this prompt made the result more useful?
cards.activity: Save a sanitized prompt in an approved team workspace. Note the task, the useful instruction and where it might not transfer. Team Trail can mark the card used; it is not a free-text prompt notebook.
cards.ai_prompt: Review this sanitized prompt and result: [prompt and result]. Suggest which instruction may have helped and where reuse may fail. Label causal explanations as hypotheses, not established facts.

cards.title: MAKE CAMP
cards.action: Summarize progress, open questions, and the next step.
cards.question: What can the next person pick up without repeating our whole discussion?
cards.activity: Say or write three bullets: progress supported by evidence, open questions and the next concrete action. Name an owner for the next action with their agreement. Keep private discussion out of shared summaries.
cards.ai_prompt: Using only these sanitized notes: [notes], draft three bullets: evidenced progress, open questions and next action. Mark missing information rather than inventing decisions or owners.

agent_workflow.label: Leave a handoff
agent_workflow.prompt: Draft a concise handoff: changes made, checks actually run and results, remaining uncertainties, and the next safe action. Do not include secrets or personal details. Do not write, commit or push it without approval.
agent_workflow.check: Another person can resume using evidence and explicit limits without reconstructing the entire chat.

tool_notes.codex: Keep stable project rules in the appropriate instruction file and task-specific progress in a separate handoff. Do not turn one-off context into permanent rules.
tool_notes.claude_code: Keep reusable project instructions separate from temporary task notes. Do not assume another person or tool shares the current conversation or private memory.

facilitator.ask: What did you notice in that attempt?
notice: Leave room for uncertainty or no change. They do not have to produce a lesson.
follow_ups: What do you make of that?
facilitator.try_invitation: Would a short progress-and-next-step summary help?
try_notice: Notice whether the summary separates observed progress from open questions. A proposed next action needs an owner's agreement; do not infer it from silence.
try_follow_ups: Does this summary match what happened?
What is the next useful step?
facilitator.optional_ai_help: AI could help organize their observations and open questions into a short summary they can correct and carry forward.

cards.title: SURPRISE ON THE TRAIL
cards.action: Compare what you expected with what happened. Name one surprise.
cards.question: What surprised us enough to change our understanding?
cards.activity: Each person may name an expectation and an observation, with passing allowed. Separate what happened from your explanation for it. Choose one uncertainty to investigate rather than forcing a lesson.
cards.ai_prompt: From these sanitized observations: [observations], separate expected result, observed result and possible explanations. Keep explanations tentative and propose one question for further investigation.

cards.title: KEEP OR ADAPT
cards.action: Name one move to keep, one to change and one thing you still cannot conclude.
cards.question: What is worth repeating, and what should change next time?
cards.activity: Review one completed attempt. Name a useful move, a specific adjustment and a limit of the evidence. If using Team Trail later, attach feedback only to the attempt actually recorded, not the team's overall performance.
cards.ai_prompt: Based only on these observations: [observations], suggest one practice to keep, one adjustment and one conclusion the evidence does not support. Avoid rating the people or team.

agent_workflow.label: Inspect the footprints
agent_workflow.prompt: Review the current diff against [agreed scope] without editing. Explain changed files, unexpected changes, risks and unverified behavior. Point to concrete locations for human inspection. Do not discard any changes.
agent_workflow.check: A human reviews the diff and can explain important behavior changes; generated explanations are checked against the actual changes.

tool_notes.codex: Ask Codex for a read-only diff review. A second review is additional scrutiny, not independent proof of correctness.
tool_notes.claude_code: Ask Claude Code for a read-only diff review. If comparing with another agent, preserve the same diff and acceptance criteria.

facilitator.try_invitation: Would it help to review one attempt together?
try_notice: Notice useful moves, possible adjustments and limits of the evidence. Avoid inferring why something worked.
try_follow_ups: What would you keep, adjust, or leave uncertain?
facilitator.ask: What is working well that you would like to keep?
notice: Make room for useful progress, not only problems. Avoid assuming you know why something worked.
facilitator.optional_ai_help: AI could help organize observations into something to keep, something to adjust, and what remains uncertain.

cards.title: TEACH THE NEXT GUIDE
cards.action: Explain one useful lesson to a teammate in plain language. Invite a correction.
cards.question: Could someone else use this lesson without our original context?
cards.activity: One volunteer explains a technique using a synthetic example. A teammate restates it and asks a question; passing is welcome. Notice what needs clarification and revise the explanation together.
cards.ai_prompt: Turn this lesson: [lesson], into a short explanation for a teammate, with a synthetic example and one limit. Avoid jargon and do not invent results we have not observed.

cards.title: TRAVEL LIGHT
cards.action: Try a fresh chat with only the essential context.
cards.question: What is the smallest context someone needs to help us?
cards.activity: Write a compact task brief with the goal, necessary constraints and one sanitized example. Start a fresh chat using that brief. Keep safety requirements; do not drop essential context merely to shorten it.
cards.ai_prompt: Help with [goal]. Necessary constraints: [constraints]. Sanitized example: [example]. Ask about missing essentials rather than guessing. Begin with one next step.

cards.title: CHANGE COURSE
cards.action: Ask AI for the strongest argument against your plan.
cards.question: What would a thoughtful critic challenge first?
cards.activity: Describe the plan and ask for a substantive objection, not an attack on people. Identify which concern has evidence and which is hypothetical. Choose whether it calls for a change or a test.
cards.ai_prompt: Give the strongest good-faith objection to this plan: [plan]. Separate evidence from assumptions and suggest a low-risk way to investigate the concern. Critique the plan, not the people.

facilitator.try_invitation: Would it help to explore a good-faith objection?
try_notice: Distinguish evidence from assumptions. An objection need not mean the plan should change.
try_follow_ups: Does this call for a change, a test, or no change?
facilitator.ask: What concerns, if any, do you have about this plan?
notice: Leave room for “none.” A different perspective is an invitation, not proof that their plan is flawed.
follow_ups: What would help you explore that concern?
facilitator.optional_ai_help: AI could offer a strong, good-faith objection, separating evidence from assumptions. They decide whether it warrants a change or a test.

cards.title: NAME THE BLOCKER
cards.action: Decide whether you lack information, a decision or a workable next action.
cards.question: What is stopping us right now, in one sentence?
cards.activity: Each person may name the blocker. Agree whether the next move is to obtain information, ask a decision-maker or reduce the task. Pick one action that addresses that blocker instead of generating more ideas.
cards.ai_prompt: Here is where we are stuck: [description]. Suggest whether the main gap is information, a decision or an actionable step. Explain uncertainty and ask one question before suggesting a move.

facilitator.ask: What have you tried so far?
notice: Hear their account before naming a blocker or proposing a fix.
follow_ups: What were you hoping would happen?
facilitator.try_invitation: Would it help to name the blocker before making more ideas?
try_notice: Notice whether the team identifies information, a decision or an actionable step it needs. Several blockers may coexist; choosing one need not dismiss the others.
try_follow_ups: Which blocker should you address first?
What action would address that blocker?
facilitator.optional_ai_help: AI could help explore their account, clarify a missing piece, or suggest another approach—without deciding the problem for them.

conditional_follow_ups.when: When they describe an unhelpful output
conditional_follow_ups.question: What part felt least useful?

cards.title: SHRINK THE CLIMB
cards.action: Replace the whole problem with one useful piece you can finish now.
cards.question: What is the smallest piece that would still move us forward?
cards.activity: Write the full task, then cross out everything not needed for one useful output. Pick a small deliverable, not a vague intention. Agree what done means and stop when it is met.
cards.ai_prompt: Break this task: [task], into a smallest useful deliverable we can finish in five minutes. Give a clear done condition and what is deliberately out of scope. Do not omit essential safety checks.

cards.title: CHANGE THE MEDIUM
cards.action: Stop editing the prompt. Sketch, sort or act out the problem instead.
cards.question: What becomes clearer if we step away from the chat window?
cards.activity: Choose paper, spoken explanation or movable notes. Represent the problem without AI for two minutes, then name one thing you could not see in the chat. Return to AI only if it serves a clear next step.
cards.ai_prompt: Suggest a two-minute, no-AI sketching or sorting activity for this generic challenge: [challenge]. Keep it accessible and offer a spoken alternative. Do not ask for confidential details.

cards.title: QUIET FIRST
cards.action: Give everyone quiet thinking time before discussion or AI suggestions.
cards.question: What do we each notice before seeing someone else's answer?
cards.activity: Allow one minute for private thinking, writing or drawing. Invite sharing without requiring it, then group contributions before asking AI. Offer a spoken or paired alternative for anyone who prefers it.
cards.ai_prompt: Using these voluntarily shared, sanitized ideas: [ideas], group similar points without ranking contributors. Preserve distinctive ideas and ask before merging points whose meanings differ.

facilitator.ask: How is working together going for you?
notice: Do not interpret quietness. Leave room for different experiences and ways of contributing.
follow_ups: Is there anything you’d like to do differently?
facilitator.try_invitation: Would a quiet minute before sharing help?
try_notice: Look for room to think independently and accessible ways to contribute. Sharing is optional; accept passing without asking people to justify it.
try_follow_ups: What would anyone like to share, or pass on?
What distinct ideas should the team keep in view?
facilitator.optional_ai_help: Offer quiet thinking, drawing, pairs, or passing. AI could later help organize voluntarily shared ideas without ranking people or inventing agreement.

cards.title: MAKE ROOM
cards.action: Offer each person a turn, with an explicit option to pass or contribute another way.
cards.question: What would you like to add, question or pass on?
cards.activity: Invite a brief round without interruptions. State that passing is welcome and private or paired contributions are alternatives. Reflect back ideas without attaching judgments to who spoke or stayed quiet.
cards.ai_prompt: Suggest a neutral invitation for a short discussion round about [generic topic]. Explicitly allow passing and written or paired alternatives. Do not pressure anyone to explain why they pass.

cards.title: PAIR BEFORE PLENARY
cards.action: Let people test an idea with a partner before offering it to the whole team.
cards.question: What feels easier to explore in a pair first?
cards.activity: Offer pairs, solo reflection or a small group. Give a simple question and time to think. Invite volunteers to share a point, with permission before sharing a partner's contribution.
cards.ai_prompt: For this generic topic: [topic], propose one clear pair-discussion question and a solo alternative. Keep the question low-pressure and do not request personal disclosures.

cards.title: MISSING VOICE
cards.action: Name an affected perspective that is absent. Record a question, not an invented answer.
cards.question: Who might be affected but is not represented in this discussion?
cards.activity: Name an absent role or access need without naming a person. Write a question for someone with that perspective and mark related assumptions untested. AI role-play cannot substitute for their participation.
cards.ai_prompt: For this idea: [idea], suggest potentially affected roles and questions to ask them. Do not speak on their behalf, infer demographic preferences or present simulated responses as actual feedback.

cards.title: PASS THE CONTROLS
cards.action: Offer a new driver and a reviewer. Keep participation optional and accessible.
cards.question: Would another role or way of contributing help someone participate?
cards.activity: Offer roles such as prompt driver, questioner, reviewer or observer. Invite a voluntary swap and agree when to check in. Do not assume everyone wants to type, speak publicly or use the same interface.
cards.ai_prompt: Suggest complementary roles for a small team doing [generic task] with AI. Include a non-typing role and an observer option. Keep role changes voluntary and avoid judging individual ability.

agent_workflow.label: Rotate the human roles
agent_workflow.prompt: For [small task], suggest a driver, reviewer and questioner role, with an observer or non-typing alternative. Keep participation voluntary. The people, not the agent, decide who takes a role and who approves actions.
agent_workflow.check: More than one person has an accessible way to contribute; driving the CLI is not treated as the only valuable role.

tool_notes.codex: The human driving Codex narrates the task and approval requests; another person checks the diff and evidence.
tool_notes.claude_code: The human driving Claude Code narrates the task and approval requests; rotate roles by agreement rather than making tool ownership permanent.

cards.title: CHOOSE THE COMPASS
cards.action: Agree on two criteria before comparing options.
cards.question: What should matter most in this choice?
cards.activity: Name two criteria linked to the team's outcome. Separate mandatory safety or policy constraints from preferences. Compare options using available evidence and leave unknowns visible instead of inventing scores.
cards.ai_prompt: Compare [options] using these agreed criteria: [criteria], and only this evidence: [evidence]. Mark unknowns and non-negotiable constraints. Do not invent numerical scores or make the decision for us.

agent_workflow.label: Agree the route
agent_workflow.prompt: Propose a small plan for [task]. List likely files, scope boundaries, acceptance checks and unresolved questions. Do not edit or run project scripts yet. Wait for our agreement before implementation.
agent_workflow.check: The team agrees on a bounded task, what is out of scope and observable acceptance checks.

tool_notes.codex: Give Codex the same written acceptance criteria the team will use to review its changes.
tool_notes.claude_code: Give Claude Code the same written acceptance criteria; a plan is a proposal, not permission to execute every later action.

facilitator.ask: What matters most in choosing your next step?
notice: Let them choose what matters; do not substitute your own priorities.
follow_ups: What tradeoff are you willing to accept?
facilitator.try_invitation: Would agreeing on two criteria help you compare options?
try_notice: Look for criteria the team actually agreed to and evidence relevant to them. Unknowns should stay visible rather than becoming invented scores.
try_follow_ups: How do the options compare on those criteria?
What is still unknown before you choose?
facilitator.optional_ai_help: AI could compare options using their criteria and available evidence, leaving unknowns visible. The decision remains theirs.

cards.title: TWO TRAILS
cards.action: Shortlist two options. Name what you gain and give up with each.
cards.question: Which trade-off are we actually willing to accept?
cards.activity: Use agreed criteria to narrow the list to two plausible options. For each, name a benefit, a cost and an uncertainty. Check dissenting concerns before choosing; do not keep generating alternatives by default.
cards.ai_prompt: For these two options: [options], summarize a benefit, a cost and an uncertainty for each using [supplied evidence]. Do not add unsupported facts or choose on behalf of the team.

cards.title: REVERSIBLE STEP
cards.action: Choose a low-risk next step you can undo. Agree when to reconsider it.
cards.question: Can we learn by moving without locking ourselves into this choice?
cards.activity: Check authority, safety and reversibility first. If the step is low-risk, agree an owner, a stopping rule and a review point. If consequences are significant or hard to reverse, seek appropriate review instead.
cards.ai_prompt: For this possible next step: [step], list questions about reversibility, authorization, risks and stopping conditions. Suggest a limited trial only if the stated constraints allow one. Do not execute actions.

agent_workflow.label: Practice recovery
agent_workflow.prompt: In a disposable practice copy, first inspect existing changes and propose one harmless edit plus a scoped recovery plan. Wait for agreement. Never overwrite unrelated work, run broad cleanup or use a destructive reset as a shortcut.
agent_workflow.check: The team can identify and undo only the approved practice change while preserving pre-existing work. A checkpoint or commit alone is not a complete backup.

tool_notes.codex: Before Codex edits, inspect repository status and agree on a safe checkpoint. Have a human review the scoped recovery action before it runs.
tool_notes.claude_code: Before Claude Code edits, inspect repository status and agree on a checkpoint. Verify the actual recovery result rather than assuming conversation recovery restores every file or external action.

cards.title: NAME THE OWNER
cards.action: Turn the choice into one next action with an agreed owner and a done condition.
cards.question: Who has agreed to do what, and how will we know it is done?
cards.activity: State the next action plainly. Invite an owner to agree, define the visible result and identify any needed permission. Put follow-up details in an approved team workspace; Team Trail does not yet store free-text commitments.
cards.ai_prompt: Turn this sanitized decision: [decision], into a proposed next-action statement with placeholders for owner, done condition and required permission. Do not assign people or invent their agreement.

cards.title: CLOSE THE LOOP
cards.action: Say what you chose, why, and what new evidence would make you revisit it.
cards.question: Can everyone tell what was decided and what is still open?
cards.activity: Summarize the choice and its rationale in plain language. Invite correction, surface unresolved concerns and name a reconsideration trigger. Distinguish an agreed decision from a proposal awaiting permission.
cards.ai_prompt: Using these sanitized notes: [notes], draft a decision summary with rationale, open concerns and a reconsideration trigger. Mark proposals separately from agreed decisions. Do not infer consensus from silence.
